$comment: HAND-MAINTAINED. There is no parser and no derivation — nothing in the concert
data can know that The Brian Setzer Orchestra is Brian Setzer. Add rows by hand.
sameAct      — one act under several marquees. Collapse them. A cover detector
that treats these as different artists produces 'you have heard
Rock This Town from four different artists' about one man.
sharesMember — different acts with a person in common. DO NOT collapse. These
are the stories, not the noise: Danny Elfman playing Oingo Boingo
songs at the Hollywood Bowl 35 years later is only a story
because they are two different acts.
Consumed only by the liner notes pipeline (scripts/liner-notes/artist-aliases.ts).
The site, the Artist scene and the MCP server do not read this file — merging the
artist mosaic is a visible product change and needs its own decision (#227 Q4).
An artist absent from this file behaves exactly as it always has: no collapse,

sameAct.name: Brian Setzer
sameAct.note: Seven shows, four marquees, 1995–2024. One man.

sharesMember.note: Stray Cats is a band, not a Setzer billing. Kept separate on purpose.
Stray Cats bassist, seen three times under his own name.
Boingo 1987–88, Elfman solo 2022 and 2026 — 35 years apart. Collapsing these would destroy one of the best joins in the archive.
Wham! 1985, solo 1988. A duo and a solo career are not the same act.
Social Distortion frontman, seen solo in 2008.
BOTAR is the acoustic project; both seen in their own right.
Berlin's singer. Appears as a setlist guest, never as a billing — the link is what lets a guest resolve to an act I actually saw.
Setlist guest only; No Doubt seen in 1988.
Men At Work opened in 2023; Colin Hay headlined solo in 2017. Two acts, one voice.
Setlist guest only; Bad Religion seen four times.
